title: Two out of three for perfect complexes
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let K, L, and M be objects of the derived category D(\mathcal{O}_X) [def-pc-derived-category]. If K\to L\to M\to K[1] is a distinguished triangle and two of K, L, and M are perfect complexes [def-pc-perfect-complex], then the third is perfect.

proof.text: Perfectness is local by [def-pc-perfect-complex]. In each of the three cases (K and L perfect, L and M perfect, or K and M perfect), intersect the covers given by the definition for the two perfect terms and refine to a common affine cover; restrictions of strictly perfect complexes to smaller opens remain strictly perfect. Fix a member $U=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$. Restriction to $U$ is exact on complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and commutes with mapping cones, so it carries the distinguished triangle to a distinguished triangle $K_U\to L_U\to M_U\to K_U[1]$ of $D(\mathcal O_U)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. By the affine clause of [def-pc-perfect-complex] (Tag 08EB), each of the two perfect terms is isomorphic in $D(\mathcal O_U)$ to $\widetilde{P^\bullet}$ for a bounded complex $P^\bullet$ of finite projective $R$-modules.

source.place: Tag 08CR, local reduction to an affine open

proof.text: Case K and L perfect: $K_U\cong\widetilde{A^\bullet}$ and $L_U\cong\widetilde{B^\bullet}$ with $A^\bullet,B^\bullet$ bounded complexes of finite projective $R$-modules. By [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] the morphism $K_U\to L_U$ is the image of a morphism $A^\bullet\to B^\bullet$ in $D(R)$, and by [lem-sc-affine-projective-complex-derived-hom] (applied to the bounded projective complex $A^\bullet$ and the bounded complex $B^\bullet$; $H^0$ of the Hom complex is chain maps modulo homotopy) that morphism is represented by a chain map $\alpha:A^\bullet\to B^\bullet$. Its cone $C(\alpha)^r=B^r\oplus A^{r+1}$ is a bounded complex of finite projective $R$-modules, and $\widetilde{C(\alpha)}=C(\widetilde\alpha)$ termwise, so the cone triangle $\widetilde{A^\bullet}\to\widetilde{B^\bullet}\to\widetilde{C(\alpha)}\to\widetilde{A^\bullet}[1]$ is distinguished in $D(\mathcal O_U)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. By (TR3) of [def-weil-triangulated-category] there is a morphism from this triangle to the restricted triangle extending the two isomorphisms, and by [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] the third component $\widetilde{C(\alpha)}\to M_U$ is an isomorphism. Case L and M perfect: by (TR2) of [def-weil-triangulated-category] the rotated triangle $L_U\to M_U\to K_U[1]\to L_U[1]$ is distinguished, and the first case gives $K_U[1]\cong\widetilde{C^\bullet}$ with $C^\bullet$ bounded finite projective, hence $K_U\cong\widetilde{C^\bullet[-1]}$, a reindexing. Case K and M perfect: applying (TR2) twice in the inverse direction, $M_U[-1]\to K_U\to L_U\to M_U$ is distinguished, and the first case applied to $M_U[-1]$ and $K_U$ gives $L_U\cong\widetilde{C^\bullet}$ with $C^\bullet$ bounded finite projective. In every case the remaining term restricted to $U$ is isomorphic to $\widetilde{C^\bullet}$, which is strictly perfect since each finite projective $R$-module is a direct summand of a finite free module.

The affine representatives obtained in Step 2 show that whichever term was not assumed perfect restricts to a strictly perfect complex on every member of the common affine cover. By the definition of a perfect complex [def-pc-perfect-complex], that term is perfect on X.
